scope: Language authoring coverage; tested_subset never means complete component parity.

components.name: Accordion
omissions: The immediate and retained C presenters have shared sizes, SVG indicators, joined cards and per-trigger styles. Python, JS/TS, Go and Rust expose copied display configuration, trigger feedback, inherited heading typography, state-specific row boxes, divider styling and queued checked changes. Retained typography uses host default or monospace faces. The five bindings also expose copied hover, keyboard-focus and press title typography and color through a separate capability. Custom headers, measured reveal and synchronous observers are immediate C APIs. Physical accessibility still needs validation.

components.name: AlertDialog
omissions: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust builders do not expose the six-slot C composition API or the Core focus-scope input cancellation helper.

components.name: Attachment
omissions: Retained C, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust expose named sizes, fitted metadata, layout and lifecycle refinements and copied RGBA previews. Configuration and preview have independent capability probes. Retained C and the five language builders enable built-in Open, Remove and Retry with an optional typed view of the existing queue. Language action events use manual polling. Immediate C, retained C, Python, JavaScript and TypeScript expose custom preview, overlay, metadata and action slots. Go and Rust builders omit custom slots. Physical accessibility remains open.

components.name: Collapsible
omissions: The immediate and retained C presenters have shared sizes, SVG indicators, outer styles and per-trigger styles. Python, JS/TS, Go and Rust expose copied display configuration, trigger feedback, state-specific heading typography and row boxes, and queued checked changes. Retained typography uses host default or monospace faces. The five bindings also expose copied hover, keyboard-focus and press title typography and color through a separate capability. Custom headers, measured reveal and synchronous observers are immediate C APIs. Physical accessibility still needs validation.

omissions.note: Packaged source SDKs carry the C paint API; language builders/bridge do not expose its style callbacks, masks, source paint policy or shadow gates. Existing tested_subset statuses describe legacy split-control authoring.

Packaged source SDKs include the additive C API; language builders/bridge do not expose custom names, tab descriptors or checked/value options. Optional toggled presence remains a separate Core/adapter gap.
Direct C accepts arbitrary loader callbacks. Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust path sources use a resource-local map of copied SVG data.

components.name: Notification
omissions: The responsive presenter, automatic first Close target and stacked action layout are direct C frame APIs. Retained builders and automatic Root submission do not expose this presentation.

components.name: Pagination
omissions: The retained C V1 bridge and all five language bindings expose named sizes and navigation options. Numeric custom height is available in immediate C, the retained C bridge, the WASM gallery and all five language bindings. Foreign builders require both optional height symbols for this operation. Retained bindings dispatch the scalar event after the frame. Synchronous typed aggregate observation is available in immediate C.

components.name: Radio
omissions: Standalone Radio and RadioGroup animation is available in immediate C, the retained C bridge, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust. All shared-provider bindings probe for the optional motion symbol. RadioGroup Item detail text appears as an accessible description. Immediate C supports decorative callbacks. The retained C bridge, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust expose an optional passive child subtree. Radio and RadioGroup option tooltips are available in immediate C, the C bridge, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust. The bindings discover the optional tooltip setter with shared providers. Signed Radio and RadioGroup tab ordering is available in immediate C, the retained C bridge, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust. Rust configures the index after creating its builder node, so probe the provider before creation for an optional index. Native system reduced-motion observation depends on the host. Radio and RadioGroup custom paint callbacks are available in immediate C. The retained C bridge, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust expose copied paint layers and probe for the optional setter with shared providers. Custom synchronous paint callbacks remain immediate C only. Standalone typed select-only boolean requests are immediate C only. Retained adapters preserve their existing queued notifications.

components.name: Rating
omissions: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust expose the optional retained Rating configuration. Earlier providers keep whole steps. The bridge and builders report queued scalar changes. Immediate C owns the synchronous callback path. Native platform accessibility acceptance remains open.

omissions.note: Direct C owns custom easing and full box refinement. Modern language facades use built-in easing and supported bridge layout fields.
Packaged sources carry the C API, but language builders retain the legacy eight-dot Spinner primitive. No source-style decorative SVG/easing/rem descriptor/reduced-motion facade is claimed.

Python/JS/TS/Go/Rust expose opt-in visual composition, density, orientation, shared design size and owned RGBA Item icons through the bridge. They retain bridge-owned selection and aggregate CHANGE; direct borrowed C descriptor arrays and per-activation controlled REQUEST handlers are not foreign builder APIs. Bridge cap remains 64 items versus C 100.

The retained bridge and all five language builders expose opt-in fill, explicit orientation, logical extents and theme indicator feedback. The immediate C custom palette and synchronous controlled request handler remain outside the builders. Retained selection keeps queued change events.

Source SDKs carry the optional C module; language builders and bridge records do not expose its typed value/state/options, sync, helpers or results. Existing tested_subset statuses describe legacy date-only authoring, not DateTime support.

components.name: Input
omissions: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust builders do not expose the native C cui_input_scroll_x query.

components.name: Questionnaire
limitations: Language builders omit C keyboard policies, snapshot copy-out and persistent typed observer attachment/payload/frame arenas. Packaged C sources and headers do not constitute a language event facade.
Localized/custom progress presentation and text refinement records/callbacks remain C-only; packaged C headers do not expose a language-builder facade.
Named text presentation policies/options, text child callback and decorative Error replacement remain C-only; no language-builder presentation facade.
Container/card geometry, numeric metric resolution, extended choice snapshots and refinements remain C-only; packaged C is not a language-builder geometry facade.

components.name: TimeField
limitations: The legacy scalar route and the optional localized builders are tested subsets in all five languages. The localized builders own their configuration and expose copied aggregate change observations. See localized_time_field_v1_source_checkpoint.

Direct C options and state, pure locale text helpers, opt-in IME preedit, the explicit Styled size and appearance entry point, and ordered frames with localized semantic text and one global stop per field remain unbound.

components.name: Dialog
omissions: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust builders do not expose the six-slot C composition API or the Core focus-scope input cancellation helper.

components.name: Popover
omissions: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust builders omit the C anchor and arrow API (cui_popover_begin, cui_popover_surface_geometry, cui_popover_position_resolve, cui_popover_arrow_resolve), cui_popover_link_trigger, cui_popover_take_secondary_press and both outside-focus begin functions. Source SDKs include the C API; builder coverage is separate.

components.name: Sidebar
omissions: The retained C bridge inherits row focus reveal from the same presenter. Custom pinned header/footer slots and Sidebar-specific scrollbar style are immediate C composition options.

components.name: VirtualList
omissions: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust support complete copied order and extent projections with optional anchoring, up to 64 existing direct Items in a vertical viewport. Earlier providers retain uniform rows. Horizontal, host measurement and larger model capacities remain in immediate C. Row focus, selection and navigation are app-owned.

components.name: Chart
omissions: The five builders use the legacy chart layout. Source point layout and optional Line markers are available through the direct C options.

components.name: DataTable
omissions: All five bindings support keyed replacement, opt-in near-end polling and opt-in capacity for up to 10,000 rows on compatible providers. Ordinary setters accept 32 rows. Custom cells and network transport are outside the bridge contract.

components.name: Plot
omissions: The five retained builders expose Plot presentation. Viewport gesture policies and physical contact evidence use the direct C APIs.

Radii are explicit; no automatic component/state radius inference.
Portable software and all five facades checked; no browser/GPU, compound-part or portal proof. Integration pending.

compound_paint_id_getters.language_builder_targets: Compound-specific builder targets remain pending; implemented control-part targets are listed separately in part_shadow_authoring_v1.

part_shadow_authoring_v1.topology: Only app root/direct dispatch through Row/Column ancestors; RadioGroup directly owns ITEM. Existing six-root API unchanged.
part_shadow_authoring_v1.ownership: Copied <=8 layers per independent physical target; MAIN aliases one slot. Empty suppresses, reset restores defaults. Whole group names every peer when any ITEM indicator is authored, even empty; last reset/removal restores legacy anonymity.
limits: No Slider thumb/fill, Settings fields, other ITEM owners, panel callbacks, portals or all78 claim.
Capability query is not presence; actual paint missing a mandatory part remains an error.
Native software/facade checks only; static package closure and other platforms use CI; browser/GPU proof pending.

limitations: Existing scalar builders retain legacy Slider behavior. Direct C Base reducer/state, owned Styled style/presentation state and result structs are not foreign-language records; the distinct bridge-owned Python/Node/TypeScript/Go/Rust double Single/Range request/receipt subset is documented in controlled_slider_v1.

The Python/Node/TypeScript/Go/Rust bridge subsets do not expose custom owned Styled style values, direct C motion state, decorative getters or arbitrary C facade options. Rust has Linux dynamic and matching bundled-static proof on1.99.1; MSRV1.85.1 remains untested.

Visible V1 gradient thumbs reject atomically; bridge/gallery V1 routes do not consume V2 backgrounds. The separate C software V2 route does not provide a foreign authoring binding. The optional C Linux adapter supports AT-SPI Set Value on typed Slider thumbs. The five language runners do not expose its numeric-mode option. Physical AT acceptance remains open.

controlled_slider_v1.scope: Copied full double Single/Range proposals in an independent FIFO; explicit receipt acceptance after step. Legacy scalar float builders and CHANGE timing unchanged. Python and Node/TypeScript own frozen records; Go owns value copies and private receipt authority and dispatches typed callbacks after legacy events; explicit whole-pair acceptance remains required. Rust owns copies and local receipt tokens, dispatching a restricted borrowed HRTB callback context after legacy callbacks; App close remains request-only and Drop owns destruction.
limitations: Native C11 owner TLS; default/shared WASM versions0. Explicit unshared final modules require trusted build assertion plus actual final-memory verification.
No native numeric AT delivery, bridge typed SET injection, V2 gradient adapter or typed-part shadow authoring.
Vertical parent-fill in registered scroll remains unsupported.
Handles/receipts remain within the matching loaded bridge image or WASM module instance; no cross-image epoch uniqueness/security claim.
Python actual-old-library fallback test skips unless CUI_BRIDGE_OLD_LIBRARY supplies an independent binary; local proof used the preserved pre-typed runtime.
Node historical optional-group tests require CUI_NODE_SLIDER_OLD_LIBRARY; TypeScript requires an existing compiler. Direct C Styled style/motion objects remain unbound.

Go tests cover dynamic current/actual-old modules and matching default embedded-source closure on Linux. Existing historical notification/shadow/visibility fixture skips are separate; first legacy run missing FontPath was retained and recovered with bundled Inter.

Copied-wire conformance is partial: Python now rejects noncanonical absent-input/repeat/nonfinite/source/inactive-numeric evidence and missing receipt authority; Go/JS/TS now reject inactive numeric evidence before publishing copied request authority; the broader inactive type-field matrix remains open. See docs/design/SLIDER_BINDING_WIRE_CONFORMANCE.md and focused validation receipts.

Rust Linux dynamic current/actual-old group, copied-provider, authored UI and matching default bundled-static source closure passed on1.99.1; MSRV1.85.1 remains a required follow-up. Historical optional Rust fixture branches are separately environment-gated; no package-release claim.

limitations: Focused root receipts cover C/Python/Node and dynamic Go/Rust. Released alpha.5 wheel, npm tarball, Go module and Rust crate have headless localized examples in scripts/test_binding_packages.py and scripts/test_compiled_binding_packages.py. Native interactive acceptance remains open.
Default/shared WASM unsupported; same existing native TLS and explicit unshared policy as controlled Slider.

Global segment Tab remains a source-focus parity exception. The direct C widget offers optional IME composition and a preedit view. The bridge and its foreign facades omit both. Clipboard and physical AT remain open.
